beliefs: f increments the last character of the input by one Unicode code point if it is a letter (any script), before inserting '4' [E1, E2, E3, E5]
f inserts '4' at index len(s)//2 of the (possibly incremented) string [E1, E2, E3, E4]
Non-letter last characters (digits, symbols, spaces) are left unchanged [E1, E4]
Increment wraps within the letter's own case: 'z'→'a', 'Z'→'A', 'é'→'ê', 'É'→'Ê' [E2, E3]
The insertion index is computed from the original string's length, which equals the incremented string's length [E1, E2, E3]
For non-ASCII letters, incrementing is by code point (é→ê, α→β, ω→ϊ, Я→а), not by case-folding or ASCII-only rules [E3, E5]
Wrap for non-ASCII letters goes to the start of the same-case run (ω→ϊ, Я→а), i.e. code point +1 unless that leaves the case-run, then the run's start [E5]
notes: E5 showed ω→ϊ (code point +1, not wrap to start of run) and Я→а (wrap to start of uppercase Cyrillic run). My v2 wrongly wrapped ω because I required the next char to be same case; but ϊ is lowercase Greek so +1 is correct. The real rule: increment by code point if the result is still a letter; only wrap when +1 is not a letter. Я+1=а which is a letter but different case, yet it wrapped to а (start of uppercase run) — so case change triggers wrap to run start. Fixed: +1 if same case and letter, else wrap to start of same-case run.
